environment.working_tree: Modified pre-existing ERP planning, contracts, run trace, migrations and delivery-validator/tests plus ADAPTER-MODE-001 Catalog adapter/storage changes and evidence updates.

decisions.summary: The Product Owner explicitly approved extending the shared Platform Files contract for the product gallery. Products will consume the shared Files capability; this approval clears only the Files-contract decision and does not authorize Product data writes/migrations or bypass the remaining security/RLS/data gates.

The authorized Platform/DB owner @loopdev-io approved an append-only Products audit event using the existing Platform event envelope, allowlisted metadata (changed field names, version, correlation ID and reason code), no field values/sensitive data, same-transaction persistence with mutation rollback on audit failure, six months active retention, and restricted archive only for documented exceptions. This approves semantics only; Platform implementation, retention enforcement, atomicity tests and all remote Products writes remain gated.

The authorized Platform/DB owner @loopdev-io approved a database-enforced global and per-organization Products write control, default false, checked by every mutation, changed only by Platform/DB owner and audited. This is design approval only; no control or migration was implemented.

The authorized Platform/DB owner @loopdev-io approved an immutable pre-cutover snapshot and forward-only recovery: disable writes/read-only on failure, repair forward without deleting post-cutover writes, and restore the snapshot only before post-cutover mutations or after reconciliation.

actions: Completed AUDIT-ENV-001: recorded repository/checkout, branch/base/HEAD, modified working tree, Vite listener and route response classification. The route returns the Vite SPA HTML shell with HTTP 200; authentication, route permissions and product operations were not verified.

Completed AUDIT-REUSE-001: shared shell/UI, Notes, Tasks, Activity and Relations are reusable; Document Intelligence is reusable only for its separate document workflows, not product-image processing. Generic Files UI/types/local adapter exist, but no approved organization-scoped remote Files adapter/association contract is implemented. The existing product-media Supabase adapter directly manages Storage, platform_files and erp_product_media_* tables, bypassing the generic Files adapter. Product Owner later approved extending the shared Files contract; the adapter still must be replaced before media feature work proceeds.

Completed AUDIT-LEGACY-001: preserve organization-scoped catalog item IDs/keys/SKUs, variants, offers/price books, CRM references and old deep links during migration; keep the user-facing Products route canonical; treat OrganizationCatalog as migration provenance only per approved decision. Current persistence has UUID-organization Supabase paths and non-UUID local-demo fallback; runtime mode/auth remains unverified.

Recorded the Product Owner's explicit approval to extend the shared Platform Files contract for the product gallery; resolved only the matching Files boundary blocker. The existing module-specific product-media adapter remains to be replaced; no Product data write or media feature implementation has started.

Rebased the legacy scope fingerprint to the normalized fingerprint that excludes task execution metadata; no approved requirement/task definitions changed. Resumed attempt 9 with no invalidated phases or approvals, preserving prior checkpoint actions, validations and evidence.
Updated delivery resume/start-phase logic to resolve only selected blockers and preserve existing checkpoint evidence; npm run test:delivery passed (34 tests).
Retried the required local migration lint against the configured Docker Supabase database; it passed with no schema errors. No remote database writes or migrations were run in this continuation.

The authorized Platform/DB owner approved the shared Products audit semantics and six-month active retention baseline. This clears the owner/contract decision only; the implementation and atomicity evidence remain behind AUDIT-SECURITY-001.

The authorized Platform/DB owner approved a DB-enforced global/per-organization write kill switch (default false) and snapshot/forward-only recovery without deleting post-cutover writes. These are design approvals only; implementation remains gated by the security and deployed-state tasks.
Re-ran the focused product identifier adapter/component tests (26 passed), application typecheck, production build and i18n check; all passed.

Audited the real local desktop Products route after the user signed in directly in the browser: canonical route renders products; legacy route redirects to canonical; Overview navigation, browser back and refresh work; the unauthenticated route redirects to login. At a 440x775 viewport the desktop renderer remains usable. Source audit found mobile has no canonical Products route and falls through to the generic workspace screen.

Completed AUDIT-ARCH-001 by comparing the Products presentation, adapters, Files boundary, capability contract and deployed policy shape with the architecture contract. Recorded existing transition debt; no new exception or production-code change was approved.

Completed AUDIT-RESP-001 by assigning current and authoritative owners for presentation, application, domain, contracts, persistence, authorization, Files, synchronization and mutation audit; documented cohesion, coupling and duplication findings with ledger remediation seams.

Performed AUDIT-REFACTOR-001 impact and recovery review: affected routes, identifier/CRM/media adapters and consumers are recorded with current regression evidence. The approved design leaves exact migration recovery and executable write-kill-switch mechanisms open, so this task remains blocked and no migration/runtime behavior was changed.

Completed the read-only AUDIT-SECURITY-001 review. It found that the new Storage write policies broadened non-product Platform Files paths from owner/admin/agent (plus matching personal upload flows) to any active organization member.

Fixed the Storage policies so only product-media paths use catalog.read/catalog.write; non-product organization writes retain the existing owner/admin/agent checks, and personal file paths retain owner/session checks. Added a forward-only correction denying authenticated physical deletion of product-media objects, plus pgTAP assertions for the policy boundaries.

The Catalog adapter suite passed (12 tests). The user applied migrations 20261025120145, 20261025120200 and 20261025122000 to loopdev-platform-dev. Remote Management API queries confirmed the versions, Storage policy definitions and authenticated Files table grants. The isolated pgTAP suite passes all 19 tests; AUDIT-SECURITY-001 and 07-build remain blocked by broader audit criteria.

Completed only ready task ADAPTER-MODE-001: Catalog backend selection now requires explicit VITE_CATALOG_ADAPTER_MODE=local_demo|supabase, fails closed when configuration is missing/invalid, and never falls back to local fixtures after remote errors. Catalog local stores use strict persistence while unrelated localStore consumers retain best-effort semantics; failed writes do not update the in-memory cache.

The decision is recorded; code, migrations, rollback rehearsal and operational tests are not implemented.

Mapped implementation and authoritative owners for all required boundaries. Recorded broad CatalogAdapter cohesion, page-to-adapter coupling, inferred runtime mode, duplicated product media lifecycle, and missing Products audit call sites, each with existing ledger remediation ownership.
